decision.reason: [ev-ffd2c3200e89] says plainly that the deprecated built-in WireGuard userspace fallback was removed, that its Helm key is `wireguard.userspaceFallback`, and that WireGuard encryption now needs a kernel with WireGuard support. But the values files of both releases [ev-28e0ccb5774a] [ev-39a22d88e2f5] do not contain `wireguard.userspaceFallback`, so the key as written cannot be found in any artifact. That means the subject path, and the exposure condition that depends on it, can't be pinned down: the real key may sit under a different or nested path. The excerpt also doesn't say what happens to a node that had the fallback turned on but whose kernel lacks WireGuard (agent failure, or encryption silently off). We need evidence of the actual values path or agent flag, and of what happens at runtime.
